change: one run reported by two writers was summed, so a 7 point exercise read 14 out of 14 and carried double weight in the points grade
_context: A teacher reported it, which is the detector this replaces. Her four students
all read 14/14 on AP Cyber 1.1 Exercise 1 under a column header of /7.
The page posts its own score as item 'redflags' and assets/apcs-score-reporter.js
scrapes the same panel and posts item 'score' through APCS_saveLessonScore.
Every reader of score_events sums per distinct item, so the pair doubled.
The percentage survived because both halves doubled; the points did not.
Same file also re-prices 1.1 exercise-2 from 8 to 15, measured off the live
page body, and adds a /api/health block that reports a column priced at one
number while its students were served another.

checks.name: the measured case, reproduced and repaired through the real routes
a corrected price reaches a container whose row already exists, and regrades nobody
the new health block sees the stale price and not the two-writer case
a second implementation, in JavaScript over raw rows, reaches the same cells
checks._why: The rule is SQL, and a suite written against that SQL agrees with it by construction. This one never touches the statements: it reads score_events with a plain SELECT, groups in memory and applies the rule by hand over generated activities.

checks.name: THE ONE THAT SHIPPED: the reader sums the carrier beside the page's own item
checks._why: This is the exact state production was in when the teacher wrote. It must go red.
checks.expect_failure: exercise-1 is 7 out of 7, not 14 out of 14

checks.name: the blunt fix: exclude the carrier outright and a one-writer page loses its grade
checks._why: This is the fix somebody reaches for next. AP Cyber 1.1 Exercise 2 records 12 out of 15 through the carrier and nothing else. Both directions have to go red or the rule is only half tested.
checks.find: WHERE se.class_id = ? AND se.course = ? AND se.item <> '${LESSON_SCORE_ITEM}'
checks.replace: WHERE se.class_id = ? AND se.course = ? AND se.item <> '${LESSON_SCORE_ITEM}' AND se.item <> '${REPORTER_TOTAL_ITEM}'

checks.name: the re-pricing proposal observes the doubled total again
checks._why: POST /api/admin/denominators/adopt AUTHORS from these numbers, so an unfixed 14 could be written in as the official price of a 7 point exercise. That is a real regrade, not a reporting artifact.
checks.expect_failure: every observed total for exercise-1 is 7

checks.name: a correction that applies whatever the stored row says
checks._why: The condition is what stops a correction clobbering a value an operator authored by hand, which is the whole reason the boot seed is insert-or-ignore.
checks.expect_failure: an operator value of 12 survives the seed

checks.name: the whole battery, per rule, one call site at a time
checks._why: Five mutations, each required to redden its OWN assertion. A mutation that reddens a neighbour is reported as a failure, because that is how a hollow guard passes.
checks.find: ok('  exercise-1 is 7 out of 7, not 14 out of 14',
checks.replace: ok('  DISARMED, this assertion no longer checks anything', true ||
checks.expect_failure: and it is THIS assertion that breaks: exercise-1 is 7 out of 7

checks.name: production reports whether a column is priced at what its students were served
checks._why: /api/health carried no `prices` key before this deploy, measured 2026-09-07 against commit 7ef7ca3. It cannot pass by accident.

checks.name: and the re-price landed: 1.1 exercise-2 is authored 15 in production
checks._why: The boot correction moves the stored row from 8 to 15. Before this deploy the value was 8 and there was no endpoint that would say so.
checks.command: curl -sS --max-time 20 https://progress.apcsexamprep.com/api/health | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',d=>s+=d).on('end',()=>{const p=JSON.parse(s).prices||{};const r=(p.worst||[]).find(w=>w.lesson==='1.1'&&w.activity_type==='exercise-2');console.log(r?('1.1 exercise-2 authored '+r.authored):'1.1 exercise-2 not reported');})"

checks.name: and the boot seed says it corrected exactly one stale row
checks._why: A correction that silently did nothing looks identical to one that ran. The seed block reports the count, and it was absent entirely before this deploy.
